title: Observable, environment objects, and passing state down the tree

videos.script: Lesson six kept the plan in one view, and handed bindings down. That works for one screen and its children. The planner has four screens. {{observable}} So the plan moves into an object they all share. The Observable macro makes a class SwiftUI can watch. And it is part of Swift, not of SwiftUI, so it runs on Linux. {{track}} You build the planner's model and then watch it. A small program subscribes three pretend screens, makes one change, and prints who would draw again. {{granularity}} The answer is exact, and it has a surprise in it. Mark a session done, and the course list redraws too. You will see why. {{owner}} Then the owner. Whoever creates the model keeps it in State. Everybody else just holds a reference. {{bindable}} Bindable, for a text field that writes into the model. {{environment}} The environment, for a model that many screens at many depths need. {{table}} One table that says which tool fits which state. {{old}} And the older way, ObservableObject, because you will read it for years.
